Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **A menu bar, in a window**: the game's menu (System, Display, the message commands, Help) shows as a menu bar above the game, as Kirikiri's Windows menu bar did. The window grows by the bar's height, so nothing is covered, and full screen has no bar. Click a title to drop its menu down, or press F10 (a controller's START or R3) to open the first one; a game's own menu (`KAGWindow_createMenus`) shows as it is, in the language shown
- **A controls list** (Help > Controls, and a Controls button on the sample's Config screen): what every key, mouse button and controller button does, read from the game's own key bindings (`kag.bindKey`), with the controller's buttons named for the pad in use
- **Screenshots**: F12 saves the screen as a PNG in the save folder, written in the background so the game doesn't stop
- **Screen readers**: on Windows, macOS and Linux, Narrator, VoiceOver or Orca reads each line out with its speaker's name, and can read and press the choices, the Yes/No prompts, About, the menu bar and the controls list
- **Positional sound**: `[se storage=... pos=farleft]`, `xpos=`, `level=` or `char=ai` places a sound on a World stage, panned to where it is and fainter further back; a looping sound at a character follows it as it moves. The Character demo plays a chime at each side of the stage and footsteps that follow Ai, with its music faded out for them, and the Animated Character demo has no music
- **Better English line breaks**: where krkr_richtext draws the message window, lines break where its line breaker puts them for the whole line, which evens out ragged lines (`lineBreakStrategy` in `Config.tjs`), and words no longer split on lines that start with a tag, have `[r]` in them or take text from `[emb]`
- kagex-release 0.12.0 downloads the 0.12.0 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.12.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
